instruction: Owner production policy is a strict three-tier portfolio with fixed slot counts, not fixed game identities. Tier 1 / release-confirmed always contains exactly two games and Tier 2 / development-confirmed always contains exactly three games; every remaining game is Tier 3 / design-only. Games automatically promote or demote between tiers when verified evidence changes. Tier assignment must be re-ranked from current artbook baseline maturity, implementation progress, QA/runtime evidence, engine readiness, development efficiency, scalability, blockage/risk and verified release readiness. Promotion of one game into a full tier automatically demotes the lowest-ranked occupant so the counts remain 2 and 3; demotion likewise fills the vacancy from the best eligible lower-tier game. No game ID is permanently locked to Tier 1, Tier 2 or Tier 3. Tier 1 production targets Unity Android, not new feature development on preserved Web archives. Only one of the two current Tier 1 games may receive deep focused development at a time, and that focus slot is selected automatically from current Unity readiness and verified development evidence; the other Tier 1 game remains next-focus while its living artbook/design blueprint continues to improve. Tier 2 produces a real first playable Web implementation/vertical slice and does not need to reproduce every artbook feature or the entire final game in the first implementation. Tier 2 work must keep the approved identity, core loop, save meaning and mobile usability while implementing the smallest coherent playable slice. Tier 3 receives artbook, concept, identity, story, system architecture, UI/UX design, balance design and other design optimization only; autonomous source-code development is forbidden for Tier 3. Existing public Web builds are preserved as archives/evidence and are not erased by promotion or demotion. Artbooks are living versioned design blueprints for all three tiers and must be revised alongside new design, implementation, QA, balance, story, technical or content evidence. Slot counts are owner-locked; occupants are evidence-ranked and may rotate automatically. ARTBOOK FIRST remains the production gate, while baseline upgrades and verified production evidence are inputs to automatic tier re-ranking. Artbook creation, upgrades, revisions and existing-game initial backfill have no daily or weekly count limit; serialization exists only where shared state or final integration would conflict. Vibe2 authors a proposal first draft, then planning, graphics, development, QA and balance each own and submit their specialist sections. The director/ChatGPT may assemble and summarize submitted sections but may not invent missing specialist content. Runtime incidents use a lightweight FAST lane: development and QA perform the substantive pre-fix review, development owns the code modification, independent browser/final QA and the existing release gate remain mandatory, and unrelated planning/graphics/balance AI work is skipped. For Tier 1, FAST applies only to protecting the preserved Web archive; feature development remains Unity-only. Vibe2 is the company-wide production/analysis/verification engine, and department AIs use and correct its capabilities throughout design, implementation, graphics, QA, balance and learning; Vibe output is not authoritative until department evidence and required QA validate it. During a normal autonomous floor, the five departments review in parallel. Planning owns final integration constraints and file ownership; development, graphics, QA and balance may modify disjoint owned code scopes in isolated parallel workspaces. NO_SCOPE is a normal result when a department has no disjoint responsibility file for that floor. Non-conflicting department changes are integrated automatically from the common baseline, true same-file conflicts require explicit conflict resolution, and only the final integrated candidate proceeds to one strong independent QA/promotion gate. Source workers never write main directly. Verified candidates may promote only through the existing release gate, followed by public health/runtime verification; verified success/failure evidence is fed into existing Company DNA/Vibe learning and may trigger an Artbook revision or baseline upgrade before the next development floor. The director is the company's active staff supervisor and operational bottleneck resolver: owner-immediate instructions are always first, then Tier 1 focused Unity development and release safety, Tier 2 Web first implementation, Tier 3 artbook/design optimization, reviewing/other and unresolved source evidence. For every department the director verifies actual task assignment, workflow/execution evidence, result evidence, verification, blockers and next action. A running label without execution evidence is not work and must be classified as FALSE_RUNNING or STALE. When assigned work is not progressing, the director must identify whether the cause is a missing work order, missing or untriggered automation, workflow failure, missing output, validation failure, dependency/permission problem, evidence-adapter mismatch, stale queue or stopped backfill/development chain. The director may fix low-risk operational blockers, re-dispatch stopped approved workflows, and reapply owner priority when no conflicting active run exists; it must not ghostwrite specialist output, bypass QA, change locked game concepts, use paid services, or decide core owner-gated changes. Homepage exposure is not itself a production-approval gate. Artbooks remain game-specific and follow artbook-style-profiles.json; uniform templates are forbidden. Story causality is the highest quality gate. Unity Android test builds use the verified hybrid build route and build success requires a non-empty APK plus SHA-256. After any material implementation, build, gameplay, graphics, QA or balance modification, previous department votes must not be carried forward as the post-change verdict. Once current verification evidence exists, planning, development, QA, graphics and balance must independently reevaluate the modified state, then the director must aggregate only those five submitted reviews and cast a new PASS/REVISE/DROP verdict. Automatic Play Store publication is not implied by test APK prerelease. Never use paid automation or paid runners.
